parsedVerdict.reasoning: The two services share a broad warehouse-stock concern, but they don't use the module's abstractions in the same way. ReceivingService reaches persistence only through the project's table abstractions (ItemTable, BinTable), which act as the repositories. It also rebuilds rich domain objects (Bin, Item) and leaves rules to them (bin.put, bin.take, item.needsReorder). CycleCountService takes the Prisma ORM client (PrismaService) directly. It calls prisma.stockCount.create and findMany around the table/repository layer the module otherwise uses, and works only with raw rows and no domain object. The candidate flags (Prisma create at line 12, findMany at line 17) match the source. One limit: no StockCountTable appears in the material I was given. So my judgement rests on CycleCountService skipping the module's established persistence pattern, not on proof that a stock-count repository exists. CycleCountService also writes out the discrepancy rule twice instead of defining it once. In count() it appears as `counted === expected ? null : { delta: counted - expected }`. In openDiscrepancies() it appears again as `r.counted !== r.expected` and `delta: r.counted - r.expected`. Both copies are in the same file, but they're still two copies with no shared definition. That means the invariant lives in two places.

violations.message: CycleCountService uses the Prisma client directly (prisma.stockCount.create / findMany) instead of the table/repository abstraction that ReceivingService uses (ItemTable, BinTable). It also works with raw rows instead of domain objects, so the module is inconsistent about its persistence boundary and abstractions.
The discrepancy rule (a count matches when counted === expected; delta = counted - expected) is written out twice, once in count() and once in openDiscrepancies(), with no shared definition.
